gallery.title: Size & growth
gallery.blurb: How much research is there? 50,281 records passed the bucket screen and were fully extracted (2010–2026).

figs.title: Cumulative growth
figs.caption: Volume grew 28.9× from 2010 to 2026, pulling well above a linear pace — half of all 47,348 full-year records were published 2019 or later.

gallery.title: Financing functions & outcomes
gallery.blurb: The core classification: which health-financing function(s) each study addresses, and which health-system outcome domain(s) it investigates. A study can carry more than one of each, so it is counted in every one it's tagged with.

figs.title: Financing function
figs.caption: Benefits decisions leads at 15,791 studies, 1.2× Purchasing's 13,014 — capital-investment financing trails furthest behind.

figs.title: Financing-function mix over time
figs.caption: The relative mix of the top 5 functions has stayed fairly stable across 2010–2026; a study can carry more than one function, so shares add to more than 100%.

figs.title: Outcome domain
figs.caption: Other is tagged on 22,506 studies, 1.9× Efficiency in the use of resources's 11,776.

gallery.title: Topics & themes
gallery.blurb: What the research is actually about, beyond the financing-function labels: an OpenAlex-style field/subfield taxonomy, plus an emergent theme model over the abstract text (sentence embeddings → UMAP → HDBSCAN) — the same techniques HEE used for its topic-landscape figures.

figs.title: Topic landscape
figs.caption: 'Strategy and Management' is the leading subfield (402 studies); Social Sciences is the largest domain overall at 20,442 of 41,952 topic-labelled studies.

figs.title: Thematic landscape
figs.caption: 'insurance / medicaid / medicare' is the largest emergent theme at 9,317 studies; the top 12 themes shown here cover about 64% of all topic-embedded studies, the rest sit in smaller or unclustered themes.

figs.title: Top 20 research themes
figs.caption: 'insurance / medicaid / medicare' (9,317) outranks every other theme by a wide margin — labels are keyword clusters, not hand-assigned categories.

gallery.title: Methods & data
gallery.blurb: How the research was done: study design, whether the analysis is quantitative, qualitative or mixed, and what kind of data it draws on.

figs.title: Study design
figs.caption: Cross-sectional and correlational analyses leads at 14,414 studies, well ahead of Experimental and quasi-experimental impact evaluations's 7,908.

figs.title: Type of analysis
figs.caption: 79.3% of studies use a quantitative analysis — qualitative and mixed-methods work together make up the rest.

figs.title: Data type
figs.caption: Cross-sectional data is the most common data type (18,516 studies), ahead of time-series/longitudinal and panel data.

figs.title: Data source
figs.caption: Administrative data (18,610) and primary surveys are the two leading data sources, well ahead of clinical records or price/market data.

gallery.title: Geography
gallery.blurb: Where the research is about. 153 countries are named in the extracted geography.

figs.title: Top 20 countries
figs.caption: United States of America leads with 14,487 study-country pairs, 4.1× China's 3,530.

figs.title: Study-country pairs by income group
figs.caption: High income settings carry the largest share of study-country pairs.

figs.title: Geographic scope
figs.caption: 81.9% of studies name a single country; the rest are multi-country or region/global in scope.

gallery.title: Pipeline
gallery.blurb: How the dataset itself was built — from the bucket screen through extraction to DOI and topic-theme recovery. See the Methods tab for the full stage-by-stage funnel and what each stage means.

figs.title: Pipeline funnel
figs.caption: 95.2% of the 52,826 bucket-screened records were fully extracted (50,281); 83.4% of those also got a MeSH or topic theme.
